title: add dynamic baseline adjustment to canary detector to handle traffic shifts
author: Daniel Park
description: Motivation: existing canary detectors assumed a static baseline computed from a fixed historical window which caused false positives during gradual traffic shifts (day/night cycles, gradual rollout traffic changes) and made rollback decisions brittle. This PR implements a dynamic baseline adjustment layer and an anti-drift guard to reduce spurious alerts while preserving sensitivity to real regressions. Key changes: 1) new baseline engine using EWMA+quantile fusion that updates with configurable decay per-metric and automatically adapts baseline windows based on observed variance; 2) per-traffic-segment baselines keyed by route+model+region to handle multi-tenant traffic patterns; 3) anomaly scoring now compares short-term window to dynamic baseline with a stability penalty to avoid reacting to transient blips; 4) new drift detector that pauses automatic baseline updates when distributional shift is detected (e.g., large median jump or data schema changes) and raises a soft alert for operator review; 5) integration with the rollout guard: canary detector emits structured reasons (baseline_adjusted, drift_paused, threshold_exceeded) used by rollout policies to prefer gradual rollback vs hard cutoff; 6) feature-flagged runtime config under canary.detector.dynamic_baseline (off by default for existing customers) and a gradual rollout plan for enabling in regions; 7) e2e test harness updates and unit tests (simulate ramp traffic, synthetic regression, and drift scenarios). Backwards compatibility: detectors keep the old static baseline algorithm behind the flag. Performance: added CPU/latency microbenchmarks for the baseline engine (expected overhead <2% for the detector process at 95th perc). Observability: new metrics (canary_dynamic_baseline_updates_total, canary_drift_pauses_total, canary_baseline_version{segment}) and tracing tags to correlate baseline updates with alerts. Testing & rollout: included offline evaluation results on the last 90 days of perf-canary data showing 34% reduction in false positives with comparable true positive recall. Rollout plan: enable feature-flag in staging, run parallel monitoring for 48h, enable in canary region for 7 days, then global. See linked Linear tasks for incremental rollout and post-rollout evaluation. Implementation notes: the baseline code lives under perf_canary/detector/baselines.py; a small protobuf schema change for detector events was added (backwards compatible via v2 tag); config lives in internal-config/canary.yaml; CI includes new unit/integration suites and a small simulation harness to reproduce common drift patterns.
